meta.audience: Alma and his people, in the land of Helam
meta.location: The land of Helam, and the wilderness toward Zarahemla

world_behind.title: Noah's priests become an education system
world_behind.text: The Lamanite king appoints them teachers over Shemlon, Shilom, and Amulon, and the record says the language of Nephi began to be taught among all the people of the Lamanites. A whole nation acquires literacy from a group of fugitives with a price on their heads.

world_behind.title: What was on the curriculum and what was not
world_behind.text: They taught record keeping and writing to one another. They did not teach anything concerning God, nor the law of Moses, nor the words of Abinadi. The record lists the omissions in that order, ending with the sermon these men had personally heard.

world_behind.title: The persecution is personal
world_behind.text: Amulon knew Alma. They had sat in the same court under the same king, and Amulon had watched him believe Abinadi and be driven out for it. The verse says he was wroth with him and then lists what he did with the authority he had been given.

world_behind.title: Prayer as a capital offense
world_behind.text: Guards are posted with orders to put to death anyone found calling on God. This is a specific ban on one act, enforced by watching. Daniel's accusers arranged something similar with a thirty-day statute.

world_behind.title: A king named for the first Laman
world_behind.text: The record pauses to note that the Lamanite king was called Laman after the name of his father, and that he was king over a numerous people. Six centuries after the original quarrel between two brothers, the name is still the throne name. The record mentions it once and moves on.

world_behind.title: Twelve days, against many
world_behind.text: Limhi's people needed a night march, a wine ration, and a two-day pursuit to get clear, and the record does not say how long the journey took. Alma's people leave in the morning and reach Zarahemla in twelve days. Both columns arrive at the same court within the same span of chapters.

words.text: Skilled and clever, with the older sense of craftsmanship shading into the modern sense of guile. Treated at 1 Nephi 16:38. The verse says the Lamanites became a cunning and a wise people as to the wisdom of the world, and then adds that they delighted in plunder. The compliment and the charge sit in a single line.

Overseers who assign and enforce labor. Every other appearance of the word in scripture is in Exodus, describing Egypt. Amulon does not invent an arrangement; he installs one the reader has already seen, and the record spells it with a hyphen both times.

Audible calling, the thing Amulon can hear and therefore forbid. The ban is on the noise rather than on the prayer. That is why the next verse can get around it without disobeying it. The word is doing precise work.

Certainty, something established past doubt rather than merely believed. Treated at Mosiah 5:2. It is the word the promise turns on, and it makes the lightened burden a piece of evidence. Knowing is named as the purpose before comfort is.
Deep, thoroughgoing. The task-masters are in a profound sleep. The record is separating their condition from ordinary morning drowsiness. The word occurs once in scripture.

Urgency, as a command rather than a description. The Lord tells Alma to haste and get out, because the Lamanites have awakened and are in pursuit. The deliverance does not come with a margin; the same voice that promised it now tells them to hurry.

phrases.term: The language of Nephi began to be taught among all the people of the Lamanites
phrases.text: A consequence with a very long reach, and the record spends eight words on it. The men who taught it were hiding from execution. The phrase appears once in all of scripture, and the literacy it describes is what later missionaries to the Lamanites will find already in place.

phrases.term: Nor did they teach them the words of Abinadi
phrases.text: The last item in a list of three omissions, and the most pointed. They withheld God, the law of Moses, and then the specific sermon they had heard preached in their own court. The record does not say they had forgotten it.

phrases.term: Whosoever should be found calling upon God should be put to death
phrases.text: A statute against one act, enforced by guards posted to watch. Daniel's accusers used a thirty-day version and a den of lions (Dan. 6:7). Both bans are about what can be observed, and in both cases the answer is that the observable part is not the whole of it.

phrases.term: Did pour out their hearts to him; and he did know the thoughts of their hearts
phrases.text: The way around the law, and it is obedience rather than defiance. They do not raise their voices, which is exactly what was forbidden. The second clause supplies the reason it works, and both halves of the phrase occur once in scripture.

phrases.term: I know of the covenant which ye have made unto me
phrases.text: The first thing the voice says, before any promise. It does not tell them their prayer was heard or their faith sufficient; it names a transaction they entered into years earlier at a pool of water. What follows is presented as the other party performing.

phrases.term: That even you cannot feel them upon your backs
phrases.text: Not the removal of the load but the removal of the sensation, stated with unusual precision. The bondage stays; the shoulders stop registering it. Nothing else in scripture describes relief in quite this way, and the clause is careful to say the burdens are still put upon them.

phrases.term: They did submit cheerfully and with patience to all the will of the Lord
phrases.text: What the lightened burden produced. The verse has already said the Lord strengthened them to bear up; this clause reports the response, and it is the response rather than the strength that verse 16 names as the reason deliverance came the next day.

phrases.term: King Mosiah did also receive them with joy
phrases.text: The word doing the work is "also." Two chapters earlier Mosiah received Limhi's people in the same words, and the record marks the repetition. Two refugee columns from the same city arrive at the same court by different roads.

verses.label: v. 3
verses.title: A king's name explained because it repeats
verses.text: The record pauses over a name it has used before: "the name of the king of the Lamanites was Laman, being called after the name of his father; and therefore he was called king Laman." The clause exists to keep a reader from confusing two men, and the volume uses the same device at Hel. 5:6 for Nephi and Lehi, at Alma 63:11 for Helaman, and at 3 Ne. 5:12 for Mormon. Four times a name is explained by pointing at the person it was taken from.

verses.label: v. 4–7
verses.title: A literacy programme, and what it did not include
verses.text: Four verses trace a chain: teachers appointed "in every land which was possessed by his people," then "the language of Nephi began to be taught among all the people of the Lamanites," then a use for it, "they taught them that they should keep their record, and that they might write one to another," and then the result, that they "began to trade one with another and wax great, and began to be a cunning and a wise people." Verse 5 supplies the exception in the middle of it: "neither did the brethren of Amulon teach them anything concerning the Lord their God." The record credits writing with the prosperity and marks the omission in the same passage.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: A persecution given a dated personal motive
verses.text: The record does not leave the cruelty general. It supplies a history: "Amulon knew Alma, that he had been one of the king's priests, and that it was he that believed the words of Abinadi and was driven out before the king." Both men were priests of Noah, and the episode being referred to is Mosiah 17, where Alma pleads for Abinadi and flees. The oppression in this chapter is between two men who worked in the same room twenty years earlier, and the verse says so.

verses.label: v. 14–15
verses.title: The relief described, and it is not removal
verses.text: The record makes the promise careful about what will change: "I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders, that even you cannot feel them upon your backs, even while you are in bondage." The last clause keeps the bondage in place. Verse 15 reports the fulfilment in the same terms, "the burdens which were laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light... and they did submit cheerfully and with patience to all the will of the Lord." Nothing about the load or the captivity is said to have altered. What is reported as changed is the capacity to carry it.

chapter.title: The ban is on volume, and it is respected
chapter.text: Amulon forbids being found calling upon God, and the people stop raising their voices. What they do instead is not defiance and not a loophole exactly. The verse says the Lord knew the thoughts of their hearts, which makes the prohibition simply beside the point.

chapter.title: The answer is shaped like the covenant
chapter.text: At the waters of Mormon they had promised to bear one another's burdens (Mosiah 18:8–9) and to stand as witnesses of God at all times. Here the Lord says he knows of that covenant, eases their burdens, and gives as his reason that they may stand as witnesses for him hereafter. Both key phrases are quoted back.

chapter.title: Relief before rescue, and the record says why
chapter.text: The burdens are made unfeelable while the bondage continues, and the stated purpose is evidence: that ye may know of a surety that I do visit my people in their afflictions. Deliverance comes second, and only after the submission is reported.

chapter.title: This settles what chapter 21 left open
chapter.text: Limhi's people fought three times, humbled themselves, were heard, had their burdens eased, and were not delivered. Alma's people pray silently, have their burdens made light, and are out within a day. The record puts the two accounts four chapters apart and never compares them, which leaves the comparison to the reader.

chapter.title: The Exodus is being rerun in miniature
chapter.text: Task-masters, burdens, crying to God, a night departure, a divinely induced sleep on the pursuers, a valley named for the leader, and twelve days to safety. The word "task-masters" belongs to Egypt everywhere else in scripture.

chapter.title: Fugitive priests give a nation its letters
chapter.text: It is said in one clause and it changes the rest of the book. The men who would not teach the words of Abinadi taught a nation to read, which is what later missionaries will build on.

chapter.title: The last thing they do is the forbidden thing
chapter.text: Verse 22 has all their men, women, and children lifting their voices in praise. The chapter opened with a death penalty for exactly that, and it closes with it done out loud in a valley named after their leader.

chapter.title: Role in the unit
chapter.text: This closes the record of Zeniff, which began at Mosiah 9. Both refugee groups are now in Zarahemla, both received with joy, and both accounts will be read aloud to the whole nation in the next chapter. What began as one colony's decision to go back has produced two peoples, two bondages, and two records.

applications.title: Notice what a prohibition actually covers
applications.text: The order was against being found calling on God. They stopped calling out and kept praying. Where you are constrained, work out precisely what is constrained before assuming the whole thing is.

applications.title: Expect the answer to match what you promised
applications.text: They had covenanted to bear burdens and stand as witnesses; the relief came in those exact terms. What you have already committed to is a reasonable place to look for how help will arrive.

applications.title: Lighter is not the same as gone
applications.text: The bondage continued and the weight stopped registering. If something is more bearable than it was, that is worth naming as an answer even though the situation has not changed.

applications.title: Submit cheerfully is a report
applications.text: The verse describes what happened after the strength came. It is not a demand made of people still crushed. Be careful about asking that of anyone, including yourself, before the burden has been touched.

applications.title: Do the night work
applications.text: They spent the whole night gathering flocks before a morning they had been promised. A promise of deliverance did not remove the packing.

applications.title: Move while the way is open
applications.text: The Lord's word was that he would stop the pursuit here, not that there would be no pursuit. When something is holding, that is the time to travel.

applications.title: Say it out loud when you can
applications.text: The first thing they did in safety was the thing that had carried a death penalty. Some gratitude is worth voicing at volume, particularly the kind that had to be silent for a while.

questions.text: What do I know that I am not passing on?
Whose good news am I angry about?
What have I stopped saying out loud that I have not stopped meaning?
What has been made bearable that I have not counted as help?
What would I name after the person who got me through?
